A1.justification: Both PDFs describe The Diffusion Duality and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Content can be matched despite the added theoretical subsection and resulting reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original Duo language-modeling, sampling, and distillation results, including component ablations and gradient-variance measurements in Tables 1–7 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains the original Duo experiments, quantitative results, ablations, and generated-text examples in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The curriculum, Rao-Blackwellized loss, Greedy-Tail sampler, and DCD algorithms remain unchanged. Equation (19) makes the tokenwise KL sum explicit under the existing sequence factorization; it does not establish a different training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use LM1B and OpenWebText for training and retain the same seven zero-shot datasets: PTB, Wikitext, LM1B, Lambada, AG News, Pubmed, and Arxiv. No additional evaluated task or domain appears.

E2.justification: The benchmark, sampling, and distillation comparisons retain the same comparator membership. Table 5's new UDLM footnote identifies the existing 36.7-PPL ablation row rather than introducing another evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model sizes, preprocessing, splits, metrics, sampling precision, and distillation settings remain unchanged. Section 5.1 attaches the existing beta/gamma window to the curriculum phase, consistent with the Gaussian-latent restriction already documented in v1 Appendix C.7.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the temperature sensitivity study, gradient/loss variance analyses, curriculum and loss ablations, teacher-weight comparison, distillation-round analyses, and qualitative samples. Expanded Appendix D.4 prose explains the existing Table 5 experiment.

E5.justification: The likelihood-estimation procedures remain the same, including the single Monte Carlo estimate in Appendix C.4 and the 1,000-sample equivalence check in Appendix B.1. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical results, and the generated-text examples are unchanged. For example, Duo's packed-LM1B PPL remains 33.7, and five-round DCD with Greedy-Tail at eight steps retains Gen PPL 69.58 and entropy 5.30.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.3 compares transition kernels and argues that discretized Gaussian trajectories need not follow discrete diffusion dynamics. Appendix A.4 replaces v1's conditional-KL proof with a divergence-contraction argument. Equation (13) now explicitly relates the reverse processes by pushforward and removes the optimal-denoiser equality assertion.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same headline contributions: Gaussian/discrete duality, doubled training speed, superiority to AR on three of seven zero-shot benchmarks, and sampling acceleration by two orders of magnitude.

C2.justification: Section 3 and new Appendix A.3 add an important qualification: matching marginals does not imply matching diffusion trajectories. This substantially limits the interpretation of the central duality beyond v1's separate-Markov-chain remark. Section 2.1 also removes the asserted equivalence between USDMs and AR training over every ordering.

D1.justification: The implementation and reproducibility information is retained, including soft embedding lookups, architecture and optimizer details, hardware, cached transformation values, data processing, and code/checkpoint access statements. Appendix C introduces no substantive technical disclosure.

R1.justification: v2 adds supporting references, including Csiszar and Cover–Thomas for divergence contraction, Han et al. for diffusion language modeling, and additional differentiation literature. Hoogeboom et al. and Ou et al. are removed alongside the all-ordering statement. The overall research positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify the background, curriculum explanation, and related work. v2 shortens the opening analogy, updates an author affiliation, standardizes notation, and inserts the new appendix subsection. The main narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 5 revises illustrative token trajectories, including the masked starting state. Table 5 gains a UDLM annotation and moves, while the existing Gen-PPL and entropy plots swap order and numbering as Figures 11 and 12. Other changes are limited reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the marginal-versus-trajectory limitation explicit and states the reverse-process assumption behind the ELBO comparison, improving the precision of v1's explanation. The empirical evidence is unchanged. However, Appendix A.4 still identifies the forward process with an argmax pushforward despite A.3's transition-kernel mismatch, so the revision does not establish a complete repair of the central theoretical argument.
